newsitem.title: SPAIN: Pleas fail to spare donkey in Spanish fiesta.
newsitem.headline: Pleas fail to spare donkey in Spanish fiesta.

text.p: A remote Spanish mountain village turned a deaf ear to a barrage of pleas from animal rights activists on Tuesday to spare a donkey from its ordeal as the centrepiece of an annual fiesta.
Activists from around Europe converged on Villanueva de la Vera to try to rescue the donkey from being forced through the streets with the heaviest man in the village sitting astride it.
But the village persisted with the ancient ritual and drunks shoved and tugged at the donkey to drive it along the streets in front of a cheering crowd.
Men fired blank cartridges near the donkey and photographers said they saw villagers forcing what was believed to be alcohol down the animal's throat.

"This is just horrendous. It's beyond belief that anyone can justify this on any grounds," said Jonathan Owen, spokesman for the World Society for the Protection of Animals. "What really is the point of all this."
But the donkey emerged better off than some of its predecessors and trotted off to the safety of its field after the hour-long parade.

"At the end of the procession the donkey was wet with sweat, tired and stressed but unhurt and in a better condition than in previous years," said Joel Gabrielli from the Paris-based Brigitte Bardot Animal Foundation.

The British-based International Donkey Protection Trust (IDPT) said last year's donkey collapsed more than 30 times on the cobbled streets as a drunken mob fell on top of him. His tail was stripped of hair.
"But this is a new donkey which is stronger and it appears that he only fell once," said Paul Svendsen, deputy administrator for the trust.

Although the origins of the festival are not entirely clear, village authorities suggested it might be linked to a traitor, rapist or Jewish man discovered during the Inquisition having been paraded around on a donkey before being executed.
Mayor Antonio Caperote denied the donkeys were mistreated and said animal rights activitists and foreigners should keep out of his village's affairs.
"I don't understand why they protest...The animal has been on his feet since the beginning and no one has hurt or mistreated him," said Caperote.
Villagers also defended the fiesta, saying the activists were spreading untrue propaganda, and harassed journalists and photographers during the procession.

After last year's fiesta, the IDPT placed adverts in Spanish newspapers protesting against the ritual . Villanueva authorities subsequently received more than 50 faxes and telephone calls in two days expressing concern, the trust said.

The trust has monitored the event since 1987 when the donkey used in the ritual, Blackie, was bought by Britain's Daily Star newspaper and taken to England to spend his final days at a donkey sanctuary.
